title: Veil and Salt
premise: Edmund Coldharbour, a cartographer who once mapped the god-realm before magic was outlawed, has hidden for fifteen years as a charm-seller in the salt-city of Greyhaven. When the old gods begin answering prayers again, Edmund learns his own forgotten bargain is the reason they were silenced—and that the last dragon, dying beneath the city, holds the memory that could either restore the gods or destroy them. Hunted by the Inquisitor Veyra and courted by a resurgent goddess, Edmund must choose between erasing his past to stay safe and revealing it to give the city back its soul. He chooses truth: he unmakes his own map of the god-realm, freeing the gods but surrendering his immortality, and dies mortal among people who finally remember his name.
about_author: Vesper Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town where the fog arrives earlier every year, and they insist this is coincidence.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Hour
chapters.summary: Edmund sells a luck-knot to a grieving dockworker in Greyhaven's night market, careful to keep every charm harmless and deniable. His POV establishes his invisibility as survival. When the dockworker's prayer is answered—impossibly—by something old and vast, Edmund feels the first tremor of the world shifting. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Salt on the Threshold
chapters.summary: Edmund investigates the answered prayer and finds the man's doorway ringed in salt that burns like scripture. Through his eyes we learn the Edict of Ash outlawed magic fifteen years ago—the same year Edmund arrived. A child begs him for a charm 'that really works,' and he refuses too harshly. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing through denial.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought Back
chapters.summary: A drowned fisherman walks out of the harbor alive, speaking in the voice of Maren, tide-goddess of the old pantheon. Edmund recognizes the miracle because he helped draw the seals that silenced her. POV shifts briefly to the fisherman's daughter, Sela, whose prayer woke the god. Emotional beat: awe curdling into terror of exposure.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Veyra, sharp and weary, begins logging miracles across the city, interviewing charm-sellers including Edmund. Their cat-and-mouse interview crackles; she suspects everyone and trusts no one, least of all the calm ones. Edmund lies well but notices she carries a page torn from a map—in his own hand. Emotional beat: hunted composure.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Edmund mapping the god-realm, his bargain with the dying dragon Emberveil to hide the gods' names inside his cartography in exchange for safety. Present-day Edmund realizes the seals are failing because Emberveil is dying. Emotional beat: the cost of survival made intimate.

chapters.title: The Congregation of Ash
chapters.summary: Sela gathers frightened believers in a cellar shrine; Edmund attends to monitor the danger and is moved despite himself by their hunger for meaning. Veyra raids the meeting, but Sela escapes with a relic: a scale from Emberveil. Edmund lets her go, betraying his neutrality. Emotional beat: belonging tempting him out of hiding.

chapters.title: Names Are Doors
chapters.summary: Edmund teaches Sela that the old gods answer true names, not prayers—a cartographer's secret. Together they speak Maren's name over the harbor and the tide rises in answer, flooding the lower wards. Wonder and catastrophe arrive together. Emotional beat: power without control.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Edict
chapters.summary: The Council blames the flood on foreign sorcery and doubles the purges. Veyra, doubting the official story, privately shows Edmund the torn map page and asks what he knows. He gives her a half-truth; she gives him a warning: someone higher wants the gods' return used as pretext for martial law. Emotional beat: unlikely alliance forming.

chapters.title: The Dragon Beneath
chapters.summary: Guided by the scale, Edmund and Sela descend into the undercity and find Emberveil, ancient and guttering, coiled around the city's foundations. The dragon reveals Edmund's bargain and the price of its death: every sealed name will tear free at once. Emotional beat: confrontation with one's younger self.

chapters.title: A Goddess at the Door
chapters.summary: Maren manifests to Edmund directly, offering restoration of his lost divinity if he surrenders the complete map. She is not cruel—she is honest about what worship costs. Edmund, starved for belonging, nearly accepts. Sela interrupts, seeing the offer for what it is. Emotional beat: temptation rendered tender.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Veyra decodes the map fragment and discovers the Edict's founders used Edmund's own atlas to build the seals—they stole his work to silence the gods. Her faith in the law fractures. She burns her ledger and comes to Edmund not as Inquisitor but as witness. Emotional beat: justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: Riot of the Remembering
chapters.summary: Miracles spread; citizens paint god-names on walls faster than soldiers can scrub them. The Council declares curfew. Edmund leads believers through hidden ways he mapped years ago, saving dozens, and for the first time uses his gift openly. Emotional beat: invisibility ending by choice.

chapters.title: Emberveil's Last Question
chapters.summary: The dying dragon asks Edmund what the map was for: to own the gods, or to free them? Edmund admits he never knew until now. Emberveil offers a final gift—one true flame, enough to unmake the seals gently—if someone carries it knowing they will burn. Emotional beat: sacrifice named plainly.

chapters.title: The Council's Gambit
chapters.summary: The Council, led by Chancellor Hesse, captures Sela and announces she will be executed as the flood-witch, hoping to bait the gods into open war and justify total rule. Veyra is ordered to stand guard; she instead sends Edmund a single line of her old ledger code. Emotional beat: betrayal at the top, loyalty below.

chapters.title: Storming the Salt Court
chapters.summary: Edmund, Veyra, and the congregation assault the Salt Court during Sela's trial. Maren's tide breaches the walls; miracles and muskets collide. Edmund reaches the scaffold as the axe falls—and catches the blade with a ward he swore never to use again, burning his left hand to scar. Emotional beat: the hidden self fully surfaced.

chapters.title: War in the God-Realm
chapters.summary: The seals rupture early; Edmund is pulled into the unraveling god-realm he once mapped, now a storm of freed and furious divinities. He navigates it by memory, the only living being who can, buying the city time as gods argue over whether mortals deserve them. Emotional beat: loneliness at the center of everything.

chapters.title: The Bargain Reversed
chapters.summary: In the god-realm, Edmund confronts the version of himself who made the original bargain, embodied in the map itself. To free the gods without war, he must unmake his atlas—erasing his immortality and his perfect memory of everyone he has loved. Emotional beat: grief chosen willingly.

chapters.title: The Unmapping
chapters.summary: Climax. Edmund burns the atlas with Emberveil's last flame as the dragon dies around him, its fire passing into the city's hearths. The gods return gently, bound by gratitude rather than seals. Maren offers him restored divinity one final time; he refuses. Emotional beat: transcendence through relinquishment.

chapters.title: After the Fire
chapters.summary: Greyhaven rebuilds with gods walking openly among it. Veyra founds a new order of witnesses rather than inquisitors. Edmund wakes mortal, his memories of the god-realm gone soft at the edges, his scarred hand aching in the rain. Emotional beat: quiet aftermath, loss made livable.

chapters.title: Sela's Cartography
chapters.summary: Sela, now the city's first licensed wonder-worker, apprentices herself to Edmund to learn mapmaking—not of realms, but of the spaces between belief and proof. Their mentorship mends his oldest wound: that knowledge must be hoarded to be safe. Emotional beat: legacy passed on.

chapters.title: The Name in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Veyra restores Edmund's name to the public record, reading aloud the full account of his bargain and sacrifice. The city that never saw him now remembers him by choice. Edmund weeps for the first time in fifteen years. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not bargained for.

chapters.title: Veil and Salt
chapters.summary: Epilogue. An old Edmund sells small charms again—but now openly, honestly, each one real. A child asks if the gods still listen; he says they always did, we just stopped asking. On the horizon, far out at sea, something vast and warm-breathed passes. Emotional beat: peace with mystery intact.
